column1: # What the space bar must do, end to end: the shipping engine, the shipping JNI bridge, the
# shipping Kotlin, against the packs the application ships. Read by PipelineTest.
#   typed <TAB> committed <TAB> situation
# `committed` is "-" when the typed text must survive untouched, which is most of this file: a
# keyboard that leaves a word alone is doing its job, and every line below that reads "-" is a
# report from someone whose word was changed when it should not have been.
# `situation` is the reason, and it is here because an outcome without one can be right by
# accident. A guard can stop working while another covers for it and the outcome stays the same
# -- which is exactly what a chain of early returns used to hide.
# --- a word still being typed is completed, not corrected -------------------------------------
# "believ" committed "belief" on a device: 4.8 times rarer, and ranked seventh by the same
# search that ranked "believe" second. Completions were barred from the corrections heap.
believ
peopl
becaus
throug
# --- a finished word with a slip in it is corrected -------------------------------------------
# The thing autocorrect is actually for, and what every guard above must not cost.
teh
wihch
aobut
# --- a mark the user typed is a decision, not a slip ------------------------------------------
# "the workers' rights" became "the workers rights"; "'hello" became "hell" once the quote was
# gone and the rest of the word was fair game. Nobody's finger lands on an apostrophe.
dogs'
workers'
'hello
'quoted
quoted'
# --- a mark left out is a convention dropped, and is restored ---------------------------------
# The opposite shape, and the one that must keep working: same character, other direction.
# "dont" is not a word, so frequency gets to decide and it becomes "don't".
dont
# "cant" IS a word -- jargon, or a slope, 108 in the pack -- so the known-word guard refuses it
# before frequency is consulted at all. kApostropheInsertCost's comment in engine.cpp claims
# this pair resolves 3,713 against 108, which is true of the engine and not of the pipeline:
# the guard above it never lets that comparison happen. Recorded as it behaves, not as the
# comment says, because changing which one is right is a decision and not a test fixture.
cant
# --- a word the dictionaries spell is left alone ----------------------------------------------
# "put" was committed as "out" on a device. Both are words; only one was typed.
put
out
form
# Refused for being too far before it is refused for being a word: the order of the situations
# is load-bearing and this is what pins it. Both answers are "leave it alone".
their
# --- an address or a filename is not a sentence -----------------------------------------------
# RunningText's job: a digit anywhere means this is not running text at all.
sha256
v2beta
# --- too short to guess about, unless an accent is being restored -----------------------------
# "ab" is in the pack, but TooShort is reached first -- again the ordering, pinned.
ab
# --- the hyphen is the other half of the mark class -------------------------------------------
# Added when kMarkDeleteCost generalised the rule away from the apostrophe, and untested until
# this file was audited against the commits: the class was widened and only half of it covered.
well-
year-
-well
# --- the first report of the whole apostrophe family ------------------------------------------
# "put'" and a space: the mark went, and "put" was already a word underneath it.
put'
# "everyone" must never become "Everton" nor "thanks" "Hanks". The dictionaries carry both names.
# The two are refused for different reasons, which is why the reason is asserted: for "everyone"
# the best the engine can offer is the word itself, so casing settles it before the known-word
# rule is reached; for "thanks" something else is offered and the rule does the work.
everyone
thanks
# "teh" must reach "the" and never "tehran", which is what reading the strip's first place did.
tehran
# --- contractions the dictionaries already hold are left alone --------------------------------
# NoChange rather than KnownWord: nothing better than the word itself was offered.
it's
don't
# Being correct is not the same as being in the dictionary. 6,910 ordinary English words are
# missing from the pack and 31.5% of them are still overwritten; "snobul" was the report that
# bought the maxEdits ceiling. Recorded as it behaves so the next attempt starts from a fact.
snobul
abaft
